newsitem.title: USA: U.S. Northeast spot power rises as cold takes grip.
newsitem.headline: U.S. Northeast spot power rises as cold takes grip.

text.p: Wholesale electricity prices in the northeastern U.S. rose Thursday against Wednesday's values as temperatures in the region began to plummet from unseasonably mild levels this week.
"Prices are up there today," noted a New York trader, adding, "They'll inch their way up depending on how much the load kicks in."

The region's temperatures Friday would run six to 12 degrees below normal in the 20-30 Fahrenheit degree range during day hours and in the teens to 20s during night hours. Weather would begin to moderate toward seasonal norms by Sunday.
Generation costs in the region remained high as both fuel oil and natural gas prices showed little signs of weakening.
In fact, swing natgas prices at the New York City gate rose to the $5.05 per million British thermal unit (mmBtu) area, up from Wednesday's $4.50-$4.70.
In the western half of the New York Power Pool (NYPP), Friday electricity for peak, non-firm delivery held in the range of $30.00-$35.00 a megawatt hour (MWh), up from $27.00-$30.00 Wednesday.
Western NYPP electricity for off-peak, non-firm delivery Friday climbed to $16.00-$17.00, up from $15.00-$16.00 Wednesday.
Prices in western New York jumped in line with a leap in spot prices in the Pennsylvania-New Jersey-Maryland (PJM) Interconnect district, market sources said.
In eastern NYPP, Friday power for peak, non-firm delivery Friday was assessed in a wide range of $33.00-$39.00, up from $30.00-$31.00 Wednesday.
Eastern NYPP power for off-peak, non-firm delivery held steady in the $19.00-$20.00 range.

The 832 megawatt (MW) James A Fitzpatrick nuclear plant, operating at low power, could achieve full output early next week. The Scriba, N.Y., facility was manually shut Sunday to repair of a leak in the electrical hydraulic control system.
In the New England Power Pool (NEPOOL), peak, non-firm electricity for Friday at Northeast Utilities' (NU) border firmed to $35.00-$37.00/MWh from $33.00-$35.00 Wednesday.
Non-firm, off-peak NEPOOL power for Friday delivery to the NU border stood at $22.00-$23.00, up from Wednesday's $21.00-$22.00.

The 910 MW Maine Yankee nuclear power plant would likely be off line well into January as the operator and the Nuclear Regulatory Commission have started a three-week review of the plant's electrical cable system.
The plant was shut December 6 after engineers found a couple of cables to the plant's main control room had been improperly routed.
